arxiv-2202-02715.title: First-passage Brownian functionals with stochastic resetting
arxiv-2202-02715.creator: Prashant Singh, Arnab Pal
arxiv-2202-02715.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Prashant Singh, Arnab Pal. We study the statistical properties of first-passage time functionals of a one dimensional Brownian motion in the presence of stochastic resetting. A first-passage functional is defined as V = ∫ 0 t f Z ⁡ [ x ⁡ ( τ ) ] V=\int_{0}^{t_{f}}Z[x(\tau)] where t f t_{f} is the first-passage time of a reset Brownian process x ⁡ ( τ ) x(\tau) , i.e., the first time the process crosses zero.

arxiv-2208-14981.title: Supercooling of the A phase of 3 He
arxiv-2208-14981.creator: Y. Tian 1, D. Lotnyk 1, A. Eyal 1,2, K. Zhang 3,4, N. Zhelev 1, T.S. Abhilash 1,5, A. Chavez 1, E.N. Smith 1, M. Hindmarsh 3,4, J. Saunders 6, E. Mueller 1, and J.M. Parpia 1
arxiv-2208-14981.description: Abstract Abstract: Because of the extreme purity, lack of disorder, and complex order parameter, the first-order superfluid 3 He A-B transition is the leading model system for first order transitions in the early universe. Here we report on the path dependence of the supercooling of the A phase over a wide range of pressures below 29.

arxiv-2301-00481.title: A low-mass hub-filament with double centre revealed in NGC2071-North 2021 A low-mass hub-filament with double centre revealed in NGC2071-North – 12
arxiv-2301-00481.creator: Vera Könyves, D. Ward-Thompson, Y. Shimajiri, P. Palmeirim, Ph. André
arxiv-2301-00481.description: Abstract We present the first analysis in NGC2071-North as a resolved hub-filament featuring a double centre. This ∼ 1.5 × 1.5 \sim 1.5\times 1.5 parsec-scale filament hub contains ∼ \sim 500 M ⊙ M_{\odot} . Seen from Planck , magnetic field lines may have facilitated the gathering of material at this isolated location.

arxiv-2308-16227.title: Black-hole spectroscopy: quasinormal modes, ringdown stability and the pseudospectrum
arxiv-2308-16227.creator: Kyriakos Destounis 1, 2 and Francisco Duque 3, 4
arxiv-2308-16227.description: Abstract Black-hole spectroscopy is a powerful tool to probe the Kerr nature of astrophysical compact objects and their environment. The observation of multiple ringdown modes in gravitational waveforms could soon lead to high-precision gravitational-wave spectroscopy, thus it is critical to understand if the quasinormal mode spectrum itself is affected by astrophysical environments, quantum corrections, and other generic modifications.

arxiv-2309-16433.title: On methods for assessment of the influence and impact of observations in convection-permitting numerical weather prediction
arxiv-2309-16433.creator: Guannan Hu, Sarah L. Dance, Alison Fowler, David Simonin, Joanne Waller, Thomas Auligne, Sean Healy, Daisuke Hotta, Ulrich Löhnert, Takemasa Miyoshi, Nikki C. Privé, Olaf Stiller, Xuguang Wang, Martin Weissmann
arxiv-2309-16433.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Guannan Hu, Sarah L. Dance, Alison Fowler, David Simonin, Joanne Waller, Thomas Auligne, Sean Healy, Daisuke Hotta, Ulrich Löhnert, Takemasa Miyoshi, Nikki C. Privé, Olaf Stiller, Xuguang Wang, Martin Weissmann. In numerical weather prediction (NWP), a large number of observations are used to create initial conditions for weather forecasting through a process known as data assimilation.

arxiv-2404-02377.title: Exploring the Impact of Source Code Linearity on the Programmers’ Comprehension of API Code Examples Conference: 32nd IEEE/ACM International Conference on Program Comprehension; April 15–16, 2024; Lisbon, Portugal 32nd IEEE/ACM International Conference on Program Comprehension (ICPC ’24), April 15–1
arxiv-2404-02377.creator: Seham Alharbi, Dimitris Kolovos
arxiv-2404-02377.description: Abstract . Context: Application Programming Interface (API) code examples are an essential knowledge resource for learning APIs. However, a few user studies have explored how the structural characteristics of the source code in code examples impact their comprehensibility and reusability.

arxiv-2406-02942.title: Light-induced large and tunable valley-selective Hall effect in a centrosymmetric system
arxiv-2406-02942.creator: Naoya Arakawa, Kenji Yonemitsu
arxiv-2406-02942.description: Abstract We propose that a large and tunable valley-selective Hall effect can be realized in a centrosymmetric system via light-induced breaking of inversion and time-reversal symmetries. This is demonstrated in graphene driven by bicircularly polarized light, which consists of a linear combination of left- and right-handed circularly polarized light with different frequencies.

arxiv-2406-15692.title: Segmenting Dead Sea Scroll Fragments for a Scientific Image Set
arxiv-2406-15692.creator: Bronson Brown-deVost, Berat Kurar-Barakat, Nachum Dershowitz
arxiv-2406-15692.description: Abstract This paper presents a customized pipeline for segmenting manuscript fragments from images curated by the Israel Antiquities Authority (IAA). The images present challenges for standard segmentation methods due to the presence of the ruler, color, and plate number bars, as well as a black background that resembles the ink and varying backing substrates.

arxiv-2407-21575.title: Cloud Collision Signatures in the Central Molecular Zone
arxiv-2407-21575.creator: Rees A. Barnes ∗ 1,2, Felix D. Priestley 1
arxiv-2407-21575.description: Abstract Molecular cloud collisions are a prominent theory for the formation of stars. Observational studies into cloud collisions identify the collision via a bridging feature: a continuous strip of line emission that connects two intensity peaks that are related in position space and separated in velocity space.

arxiv-2506-15778.title: Twisted-Circle Compactifications of SQCD-like Theories and Holography
arxiv-2506-15778.creator: Niall T. Macpherson
arxiv-2506-15778.description: Abstract Abstract We construct and analyse holographic duals to a class of four-dimensional \mathcal{N}=1 SU (N_{c}) SQCD-like theories compactified on a circle with an R-symmetry twist. The setup originates from type IIB backgrounds previously proposed as duals to SQCD with N_{f} fundamental flavours. The U(1) R-symmetry is anomaly-free only if N_{f}=2N_{c} .

pmc-10654956.title: Hospital-onset bacteremia and fungemia: examining healthcare-associated infections prevention through a wider lens
pmc-10654956.creator: Gregory M. Schrank, Graham M. Snyder, Surbhi Leekha
pmc-10654956.description: A hospital-onset bacteremia and fungemia (HOB) metric will expand hospital surveillance of bloodstream infections beyond current state and provide an opportunity to re-evaluate infection prevention strategies. Here we consider the added value and potential pitfalls of HOB surveillance and present a framework for the standardized assessment of HOB events.

pmc-12418167.title: Deciphering the Genetic Association Between the FODMAP Diet and Recurring Oral Aphthae—The Mediating Role of Ferroptosis
pmc-12418167.creator: Baolin Jia, Xiaojuan Wu, Qiang Wang, Jun Ren, Guixin Li, Xianjie Zheng, Sen Yang
pmc-12418167.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). The incidence of recurrent oral aphthae (ROA) is on the rise. Its etiology is unknown, particularly its relationship with the FODMAP diet. This investigation delved into their genetic correlation and elucidated the role of ferroptosis. Two‐sample Mendelian randomization (MR) analysis was performed, and mediation MR analysis to investigate the relationship between the FODMAP Diet, Ferroptosis, and ROA using GWAS data from Finngen for ROA, deCODE for ferroptosis, and UKB for the FODMAP Diet.

pmc-12440896.title: Associations between structural holes in personal networks and health behaviors among young and middle-aged adults in Japan: a population-based cross-sectional study
pmc-12440896.creator: Yasutaka Kuribayashi, Daisuke Takagi
pmc-12440896.description: Previous studies have emphasized that tightly knit networks influence health behaviors. However, effective network structures for behavioral adoption may vary by diffusion stage. This study examines how the association between personal network structures and health behaviors varies across behaviors with different prevalence degrees.

pmc-12539965.title: Interview-based sighting history to investigate the historical range and dynamics of dugongs in China
pmc-12539965.creator: Mingli Lin, Yuanyuan Li, Yifei Cai, Haozhong Chen, Zirui You, Ouhoud Soufiane, Songhai Li
pmc-12539965.description: The dugong (Dugong dugon) is the first marine megafauna to be declared functionally extinct in China, yet its historical range and extinction dynamics remain poorly understood. Sighting histories were thus collected from 841 fishers to investigate this information based on a large-scale interview survey across the entire dugong historical range in 2024.

pmc-12612013.title: Computer-assisted total hip arthroplasty reduces early complications based on Japanese nationwide medical claims data
pmc-12612013.creator: Hidetatsu Tanaka, Kunio Tarasawa, Yu Mori, Hiroaki Kurishima, Hiroki Kawamata, Kiyohide Fushimi, Kenji Fujimori, Toshimi Aizawa
pmc-12612013.description: Introduction: Computer-assisted (CA) surgery is increasingly adopted in total hip arthroplasty (THA) to enhance implant positioning accuracy. However, robust evidence regarding its impact on postoperative complications compared with manual THA (M-THA) remains limited. This study evaluated the association between CA-THA and early postoperative complications using a large Japanese database.

pmc-13239459.title: What are the characteristics and impacts of a patient-led conference? A qualitative study
pmc-13239459.creator: Tianna Magel, Kimberly Strain, Anna Samson, Dawn P Richards, Hetty Mulhall, Karim M Khan, Lorelei Lingard
pmc-13239459.description: AbstractBackgroundPatient engagement is the practice of “meaningful and active collaboration [of patient partners] in governance, priority setting, conducting research and knowledge translation.” Patient engagement has been implemented in various settings including clinical, research, and quality improvement, with varying levels of patient contributions and decision-making responsibility.

pmc-13398062.title: Geriatric Oral Health in the United States: Current Status and Challenges
pmc-13398062.creator: Sherif Ammar, Frederick Howard, Xi Chen, Duangporn Duangthip
pmc-13398062.description: The United States is experiencing rapid population aging, making geriatric oral health an increasingly important public health and clinical concern. Older adults bear a disproportionate burden of oral diseases, including dental caries, periodontal disease, edentulism, xerostomia, and oral cancer, many of which are closely linked to chronic systemic conditions such as diabetes, cardiovascular disease, and cognitive impairment.
